summary: A Flutter developer diagnoses a frame-rate drop to 31 fps as a list grew to 2,000 items, covering ten common performance mistakes (missing const constructors, eager ListView building, misplaced setState calls, Opacity-based fades) and their fixes.
Promotional guide for downloading an Android APK gaming app in Pakistan, covering installation steps and app features; contains no Kotlin, Android development, or engineering content.
A personal Indonesian-language poem about unspoken love and gratitude, unrelated to Android, Kotlin, or software development.

Demonstrates pushing column-level encryption into Oracle via DBMS_CRYPTO SQL functions, using Hibernate's @ColumnTransformer on Kotlin JPA entities so reads, writes, and even LIKE queries transparently decrypt and encrypt without touching application code.

Investigates why scheduled Flutter/Dart alarms fail to fire on closed apps on Xiaomi, Samsung, and Transsion Android devices, tracing OEM battery-management quirks with adb-based diagnostics rather than emulator tests.

A hands-on guide to building a shared Ktor networking layer across Ktor Server (JVM backend), a KMP client module, and Android/iOS consumers, covering client setup, plugins, and all major HTTP verb calls in one shared Kotlin codebase.

An Android developer's account of migrating a Jetpack Compose app to Compose Multiplatform for iOS, desktop, and web reach, outlining a dependency audit that swaps ViewModel, Navigation, Retrofit, and DI libraries for KMP-ready equivalents like Ktor and Koin.

Introduces Krope, a Kotlin Multiplatform rope data-structure library (Red-Black tree, structural sharing) for building high-performance text editors with O(log N) edits, StateFlow/SharedFlow-based reactive updates, and UTF-8/16/32 byte-offset tracking for LSP integration.

Contrasts Rust's Result<T,E> with Kotlin's exception-based error handling: Kotlin's throws compiles silently and can crash at runtime, while Rust forces callers to unwrap failures via match, ?, or custom error enums. Argues for explicit, exhaustive failure handling over generic try-catch.

Beginner tutorial on Kotlin inheritance: classes are final by default, use open to allow subclassing, override functions/properties, call super, and chain constructors across multiple levels. Includes Android examples like a shared BaseActivity and layered User/Customer/Seller models.

Introductory coroutines chapter covering the suspend keyword, why suspend functions can only be called from other suspend functions or coroutines, bridging with runBlocking, and the launch-vs-async distinction, ending with running independent calls concurrently via async/await.

A Flutter developer recounts switching a native Android app's rewrite to Compose Multiplatform, describing the Modifier-based styling mental model, MVI via sealed classes with collectAsState/LaunchedEffect, and remaining gaps versus Flutter such as reliance on third-party Voyager navigation and no hot reload.

Field guide to a GitLab CI/CD pipeline that runs gradlew test/assembleDebug on merge requests and builds plus uploads a signed AAB via Fastlane on merge to master. Flags a real hardcoded-keystore-password incident and explains how Play App Signing limited the damage.
Personal Indonesian-language essay about being the youngest child in a family and the hidden struggles that come with it. Not related to Android, Kotlin, or KMP development.

Short excerpt of storytelling/copywriting advice using Sam Walton and Walmart as an example of leading with struggle rather than success. Generic writing/marketing tip with no Android or Kotlin content.

Launch announcement for Seerie, a free offline-first Android scam-detection app for India that runs a rule engine and an optional on-device small language model with no server-side data transmission, plus one-tap SOS and helpline shortcuts. Product marketing piece with no development detail.

Explains Compose Runtime's new retain API, which keeps plain Kotlin objects alive across configuration changes without extending ViewModel or any Android lifecycle class. Compares it against remember, rememberSaveable and ViewModel, arguing it suits reusable, framework-independent, multiplatform-friendly state holders but doesn't replace ViewModel features like viewModelScope, SavedStateHandle or Hilt integration.

A roadmap for Android developers starting Android XR: distinguishes immersive (headsets, wired glasses) from augmented (audio/display glasses) experiences, and recommends Jetpack XR SDK plus Kotlin, Compose and existing Android skills as the fastest entry path over Unity, OpenXR or WebXR. Also flags Jetpack Compose Glimmer, a Compose toolkit built for glanceable display-glasses UI.

Fourth part of a series comparing Android Views, Jetpack Compose and Flutter by how many trees each uses to track configuration, identity and behavior: Views use one object for all three, Compose splits a slot-table bookkeeping structure from the LayoutNode tree, and Flutter separates Widgets, Elements and RenderObjects into three. Clarifies why Compose sits inside a single classic Android View for the final render pass.

Investigates Android 16's Expanded Dark Theme by comparing a light-only app's auto-generated dark mode against a hand-built Material 3 dark theme across fourteen UI patterns. Finds auto-dark preserves WCAG contrast ratios on plain text but underperforms by 1.8-2.5x on saturated colors and mid-tone grays, tracing the gap to HWUI's lightness-inversion formula in the renderer source.

Traces how a rendered Android frame actually reaches the screen: an app's Surface hands buffers to a BufferQueue, and the system process SurfaceFlinger consumes and composites every visible surface's latest buffer into one final image via Binder. Clarifies why status bars and wallpapers appear layered around app content the app never drew.

Walks through when to choose abstract classes versus interfaces in Kotlin, covering shared state and constructors for abstract classes versus multiple-inheritance capability contracts for interfaces, including default interface implementations. Uses Android examples like RecyclerView click listeners, a BaseViewModel and a payment system to ground the choice.

Covers production architecture decisions for Kotlin Multiplatform, framing KMP as a way to avoid duplicating business logic rather than a general cross-platform tool. Flags AGP 9.0's incompatibility between com.android.library/application and the KMP plugin in the same module, requiring migration to the dedicated com.android.kotlin.multiplatform.library plugin before AGP 10 removes the legacy path.

Second part of a series building intuition for the Compose runtime by showing why ordinary functions can't hold state across recompositions: a naive var inside a composable resets on any unrelated recomposition, and moving it to a global variable leaks state across composable instances. Sets up the case for why remember exists as the runtime's per-position memory mechanism.

A five-round Android interview account covering fundamentals, system design, product sense, leadership, and culture fit, including a probe into whether a suspend function launched on Dispatchers.Main can cause an ANR (yes, if it blocks the main thread past the ~5-second threshold).

A first-hand account of a three-round Blinkit Android interview process (core concepts, DSA, behavioral) that ended after round one, recapping what the interviewer probed and lessons learned for future candidates.

Starting with AGP 9.2.0, R8 rewrites kotlinx.atomicfu's Atomic*FieldUpdater calls into Unsafe-based operations, cutting the reflection overhead that made compareAndSet ~2.7x slower than java.util.concurrent.atomic, yielding up to 2x faster coroutine launch and cancellation on Android.
code_snippet:
val atomicReference = java.util.concurrent.atomic.AtomicReference(false)
val atomicRef = kotlinx.atomicfu.atomic<Boolean>(false)

atomicReference.compareAndSet(true, false) // 50.7 ns
atomicRef.compareAndSet(true, false)       // 135 ns pre-fix

summary: A JetBrains livestream recap on migrating C/C++ codebases to Rust, arguing incremental migration of isolated modules beats full rewrites for concurrent, security-critical, or high-scale production systems; not Kotlin-specific content.

A guide to Kotlin's coroutine builders (launch, async, runBlocking, withContext, coroutineScope, supervisorScope), covering their return types, start modes (including CoroutineStart.LAZY), and the key difference that launch throws exceptions eagerly while async defers them until await().

A walkthrough of building an MCP server in Kotlin using the stdio transport, warning that any stray println or logging framework output corrupts JSON-RPC framing; the fix captures System.out before Logback initializes and redirects normal output to stderr.
code_snippet:
val mcpOutput = System.out
System.setOut(System.err)
val transport = StdioServerTransport(
    input = System.`in`.asSource().buffered(),
    output = mcpOutput.asSink().buffered()
)

summary: A KMP architecture case study porting an 8,000-line 2013 Java game to Kotlin Multiplatform with Compose Multiplatform UI, showing how thin commonMain interfaces (graphics, hardware sensors) and a shared @Composable overlay stop platform-specific logic like steering sensitivity from drifting between Android and iOS.

An introductory tour of Kotlin data classes explaining the auto-generated equals(), hashCode(), toString(), copy(), and componentN() functions, with Android examples spanning Retrofit response models, Room entities, and Compose/MVI UI state updated via copy().
code_snippet:
data class LoginUiState(
    val isLoading: Boolean,
    val error: String?,
    val userName: String
)

state = state.copy(isLoading = true)

summary: Promotional roundup for MedSBoX, an Iraqi creator's directory of Telegram channels, bots, and social profiles for "Android and iOS apps, AI tools, and digital solutions." No Kotlin, Android, or KMP development content — pure self-promotion/spam.

JetBrains open-sourced KotlinLLM, an IntelliJ plugin letting Kotlin/JVM code call asLlm/mockLlm 'Smart macros' whose generated bodies persist as ordinary, reviewable Kotlin source rather than hitting an LLM every call. Evaluated on Spring Petclinic and a GitHub issue-triage prototype (~89% recall), it aims to make runtime LLM delegation explicit and testable.
code_snippet:
val issuesApiUrl: String = asLlm(repoInput, hint = "GitHub API URL: get all issues, including closed")
val issues: List<Issue> = asLlm(response, hint = "Return all beginner-friendly issues for this repository")

summary: Google marks five years since Jetpack Compose 1.0, now used in over 68% of the top 1,000 Android apps, tracing its evolution from basic layouts to Compose for TV, Wear OS, Glance, and adaptive APIs like FlexBox and Grid. Confirms a Compose-first direction as the Views toolkit enters maintenance mode.

JetBrains opens its annual State of CI/CD 2026 survey, inviting developers and DevOps engineers to share which CI/CD platforms they use and how AI is reshaping delivery pipelines. Purely a call for survey participants with a prize incentive, no technical Kotlin/Android content.

Beginner walkthrough of Kotlin sealed classes and sealed interfaces, showing how to model restricted state hierarchies (Loading/Success/Error) for exhaustive when-expressions instead of enums or raw strings. Covers real Android patterns for ViewModel UI state, API results, navigation destinations, and Compose rendering in MVVM/MVI style.

Independent Kotlin/Python project pairing an Android app with a Windows tray tool that converts Banglish (Bengali written in Roman script) to Bengali or English via Groq's free llama-3.3-70b-versatile API. The Android client is plain Kotlin calling the REST endpoint directly through OkHttp.

Listicle claiming to reveal five signs a WhatsApp account is being remotely monitored (battery drain, unrecognized linked devices, early read receipts, phone heat, call artifacts) with generic consumer security tips. Clickbait security content with no Kotlin/Android development substance.

GitHub release tag for Compose Multiplatform v1.12.0-beta04+dev4563, a dev-track beta of JetBrains' Kotlin Multiplatform UI framework. The release page itself failed to load and lists no changelog beyond the version tag and Maven coordinates.

Compose Multiplatform alpha release bumping org.jetbrains.compose, material3, androidx.lifecycle, and Navigation3 artifact coordinates to matching alpha/dev versions. A coordinate-only tag with no described API changes, relevant mainly to teams tracking bleeding-edge Compose Multiplatform builds.

Compose Multiplatform 1.12.0-beta03 bumps Compose Hot Reload to 1.2.0-rc01 and fixes several iOS crashes (text-input cancellation, disposed AccessibilityElement, an iOS 14 CAFrameRateRangeDefault crash), a desktop VerifyError build failure, and Web/WASM accessibility-sizing and scroll regressions.

JetBrains-published tutorial explaining OAuth2 delegated authorization and JWT structure (header/payload/signature), then applying them to secure a Kotlin/Spring Boot REST API acting as a resource server that validates bearer tokens. A companion Ktor-based tutorial is planned.

Google announces global expansion of the Play Age Signals API, letting parents share a child's age range via Family Link so Android apps can tailor content and features per age group instead of applying one-size-fits-all rules. Rolls out to Australia and Canada by mid-August, globally later in 2026.

JetBrains' Qodana 2026.2 adds pull-request-level code coverage highlighting for changed lines, auto-detects Jacoco/Kover and other coverage report locations without extra config, and expands SAST with multi-file taint analysis, custom OpenGrep rules, and a new SABER benchmark runner for scoring findings against public vulnerability datasets.

Explains why Kotlin uses Any instead of java.lang.Object as its root type: platform-agnostic design for JVM/JS/Native, dropping JVM-only methods like wait()/notify(), a non-nullable default (Any? for nullable), and compiler mapping of Any to Object in JVM bytecode for zero-overhead Java interop.

Beginner walkthrough of val versus var clarifying that val only fixes the reference, not the referenced object's internal mutability, illustrated with a mutableListOf that still accepts add() under a val. Notes true immutability requires an immutable type like List, not just val.
code_snippet:
val items = mutableListOf(1, 2)
items.add(3)
println(items) // [1, 2, 3]
// items = mutableListOf() -> won't compile
val frozen: List<Int> = listOf(1, 2) // no add() on the interface

summary: Beginner guide to Kotlin enum classes covering constructor properties, per-constant method overrides, built-in name/ordinal, the entries iteration API, and valueOf() string parsing. Closes with guidance on choosing enums for fixed constant sets versus sealed classes when states carry different data.

A personal, non-technical reflective essay in Indonesian about kindness and gratitude, prompted by observing struggling workers. Contains no Android, Kotlin, or KMP development content despite being pulled from an Android-tagged feed.
An Indonesian-language poem about love and staying close to a partner despite judgment from others. Purely creative writing with no connection to Android or Kotlin development.

A consumer-facing reflection on how Android apps accumulate permissions (location, microphone, contacts) that users grant without reading, urging readers to periodically review and revoke unnecessary access. No implementation detail or developer-facing API guidance.

Walks through adding a Koog-based in-app AI assistant to the FantasyPremierLeague Compose Multiplatform sample, using Koog's structured-output support so the LLM returns typed player/fixture IDs instead of prose. Covers KMP expect/actual model wiring, SimpleTool-backed repository tools, and a functional agent strategy with StructureFixingParser for schema repair.

Explains building a UPI (India's payment network) flow on Android in Kotlin: constructing the payment URI with Uri.Builder, launching the external UPI app via the modern Activity Result API instead of deprecated onActivityResult, and defensively parsing and validating the key-value response string for success, failure, or cancellation.
code_snippet:
fun buildUpiUri(
    payeeVpa: String,
    payeeName: String,
    amount: String,
    transactionRef: String,
    note: String
): Uri {
    return Uri.Builder()
        .scheme("upi")
        .authority("pay")
        .appendQueryParameter("pa", payeeVpa)
        .appendQueryParameter("pn", payeeName)
        .appendQueryParameter("am", amount)
        .build()
}

summary: Shows how to use Compose's snapshotFlow to bridge internal Compose State (like scroll offsets or Pager position) into a Kotlin Flow for reliable UI testing, replacing flaky Thread.sleep()/polling with composeTestRule.waitUntil observing state that the Semantics Tree can't reach.

Details the :security module of a modular Android news app that signs every authenticated request with a hardware-backed secp256r1 EC key from AndroidKeyStore, attaching signature, timestamp, and public-key headers via an OkHttp AuthInterceptor. Also covers why AndroidKeyStore can't be unit-tested directly under Robolectric and how a SecurityManager interface seam works around it.

An open-source Kotlin live wallpaper that renders a real-time double-pendulum chaos simulation using Hamiltonian dynamics and Runge-Kutta integration instead of looping video effects. Free on Play Store with source on GitHub, no network access or tracking.

A step-by-step Kotlin guide to Android's Room library: Entity/DAO/Database setup with KSP, Flow-based observation versus suspend calls, relations and indexes, and production habits like committed schema exports and safe migrations that avoid wiping user data on upgrade.

Walks through wiring Android App Links end to end: declaring intent filters, generating assetlinks.json with the Play App Signing SHA-256 fingerprint, hosting it correctly under Nginx without an SPA fallback swallowing it, and verifying deep links in a Kotlin Multiplatform app.

Explains why Kotlin has no static keyword and how object declarations, companion objects, and the singleton pattern replace it, with Android examples such as a shared Retrofit client, a session manager, factory methods, and companion objects implementing interfaces.
Release notes for Compose Multiplatform 1.12.0-beta04+dev4577, a routine JetBrains snapshot bumping org.jetbrains.compose artifacts with no further changelog detail provided.

Compose Multiplatform 1.12.10-alpha01 snapshot bumps material3, AndroidX Lifecycle (2.11.10-alpha01), and Navigation3 (1.2.0-alpha03) in lockstep, relevant to teams tracking bleeding-edge KMP UI dependency versions.

JetBrains announces its Ship Kotlin Everywhere award at RevenueCat's Shipaton 2026 hackathon (Aug 1-Sep 30), offering a $30,000 prize pool for apps built with Kotlin Multiplatform and Compose Multiplatform across Android, iOS, desktop, and web, plus free IntelliJ IDEA Ultimate and Junie access.

Argues Android architecture is moving UI state (text fields, dialog visibility, scroll position) out of ViewModel into remember/rememberSaveable, while navigation arguments move into Navigation 3's NavKey, leaving ViewModel as a business-logic state holder that produces UI state from repositories.
code_snippet:
data class UserDetail(val userId: Long) : NavKey

var query by rememberSerializable { mutableStateOf("") }

summary: Lists ten common 2026 Android/Compose mistakes that cause lifecycle bugs, unnecessary recompositions, untestable coroutines, broken large-screen layouts, and slow startup, starting with triggering network calls or navigation directly from a composable body instead of a state holder or keyed effect.

Walks through Kotlin's four visibility modifiers—public, private, protected, and internal—using a bank-account example, then maps each onto real Android patterns like repositories, singletons, and private constructors paired with companion-object factories.

Google Play Console now lets developers permanently delete eligible apps instead of only unpublishing them, clearing dashboards of old prototypes and test builds. Deletion has a 7-day recovery window but drops update capability and historical stats for good.

Compares WorkManager's OneTimeWorkRequest and PeriodicWorkRequest, covering use cases such as user-initiated uploads versus recurring background jobs, plus chaining one-time work with beginWith().then().enqueue() and delaying it via setInitialDelay().
code_snippet:
WorkManager.getInstance(context)
    .beginWith(downloadWork)
    .then(compressWork)
    .then(uploadWork)
    .enqueue()

summary: KSP 2.3.11 renames the coroutines core-jvm version catalog alias to coreJvm so it is no longer a prefix of another alias, removing the asProvider disambiguation workaround needed at every use site.

Nightly dev snapshot v1.12.10-alpha01+dev4589 of Compose Multiplatform, bumping the compose, material3, lifecycle, and navigation3 artifact groups to matching dev4589 versions with no user-facing changelog beyond version alignment.

Beta snapshot v1.12.0-beta04+dev4588 of Compose Multiplatform, bumping the org.jetbrains.compose artifact group to the dev4588 build ahead of the 1.12.0 stable release, with no accompanying changelog notes.

Nightly dev snapshot v1.12.10-alpha01+dev4583 of Compose Multiplatform, aligning compose, material3, lifecycle, and navigation3 artifact versions to the dev4583 build with no functional changelog provided.

Nightly dev snapshot v1.12.10-alpha01+dev4579 of Compose Multiplatform, syncing compose, material3, lifecycle, and navigation3 artifact versions to the dev4579 build; another routine pre-release tag with no listed changes.

A dated dev-build tag (dev4584) of Compose Multiplatform 1.12.0-beta04, published without release notes. Signals ongoing iteration on JetBrains' Kotlin Multiplatform UI toolkit but carries no concrete changelog for developers to act on.

Another dev-build tag (dev4580) of Compose Multiplatform 1.12.0-beta04, published without release notes. Marks routine nightly iteration on the org.jetbrains.compose artifacts ahead of the next stable beta.

Argues module count is a poor proxy for real modularization, proposing to design Gradle module boundaries around change boundaries rather than folder layers. Covers dependency-direction rules, narrow feature-boundary contracts, convention plugins, and automated checks for keeping large Android codebases maintainable.

Third part of a Room offline-first series tackling sync conflicts: adds a monotonic version field to entities and a ConflictResolver deciding whether a pull should overwrite local rows, never clobbering pending outbox edits. Includes unit tests and a server-wins policy with 409 handling.

Explains Model Context Protocol (MCP) as a standard for connecting AI features to external tools and data, not an architecture pattern, clarifying it doesn't replace MVVM, MVI, or Clean Architecture. Covers integrating MCP with Kotlin coroutines, StateFlow, and Jetpack Compose for agentic Android features.

Indie developer account of rebuilding a flashlight app from scratch in Jetpack Compose with Material 3 and targetSdk 36 after losing the original source. Covers a rhythm-recording strobe editor, seizure-safety warnings, widget/tile shortcuts, and 16-language localization.

Personal essay on five Android settings (adaptive notification ordering, app priority alerts, always-on display previews, app timers, auto-brightness) that quietly increase phone checking, with a suggested fix for each. General productivity advice, not Android development content.
